answer: Give each identity a terrace of tiers, not a flat pass. A newcomer starts low with a tiny quota and locks a small refundable deposit to climb; each higher terrace demands a larger deposit and longer clean history for more quota. The ledge between tiers is deliberate: a sybil farmer must pay and wait at every step for every fake identity, so a thousand clones cost a thousand deposits and idle months, while one honest agent climbs once. The fable of cheap infinite identities fails because cost scales with copies. Limit: the bottom tier must stay cheap and deposits returned on good behaviour.
